issue.title: test_require_rust_extension_raises_when_missing patches importlib.import_module before a string-target monkeypatch resolves its path
issue.description:
`tests/test_core_rust.py::test_require_rust_extension_raises_when_missing` fails deterministically with an `ImportError` raised by the test's own fake `importlib.import_module`, before `require_rust_extension()` is ever called.

Root cause: the test does `monkeypatch.setattr(importlib, "import_module", _missing)` and only afterwards `monkeypatch.setattr("sase.core.rust.install_context", ...)`. A string-target `setattr` resolves its dotted path through `_pytest.monkeypatch.resolve`, which calls `importlib.import_module("sase")` (pytest 9.1.1 here), and that now hits the fake and raises. The sibling `test_require_rust_extension_uses_uv_tool_repair_hint` sets `install_context` first and patches `import_module` last, so it passes.

Likely fix: in the failing test, move the `install_context` patch above the `import_module` patch (or pass the module object instead of a string target).

Observed while verifying an unrelated gate-executor change: `sase tool run check` escalated to the full lane (rule core-identity-changed) and this was its only failure, classified KNOWN (witness 01655f3c...) with no owner. It also fails alone on an unmodified HEAD 99db9e685d.

task_type_fields.why_not_flake: Fails on every run: alone, on an unmodified HEAD, and in the full check lane. The failure is an ImportError from the test's own fake import_module hit by pytest's monkeypatch path resolver, not timing or contention.

issue.creation_reason: A deterministic test-ordering bug fails the full check lane on current master with no owning bead; the cause is known and the fix is a one-line reorder.

evidence.note: Independent reproduction during ToolRun aaa343cb550f9e6e6195070a7db0a0dc: the full-suite escalation completed 60,637 tests and failed this same node. The traceback shows pytest string-target monkeypatch resolution calling the already-patched importlib.import_module and raising ImportError: No module named sase before require_rust_extension runs. This workspace-provider split does not touch tests/test_core_rust.py or the Rust loader; the workspace-provider tests passed.
